Question: Why did the Aam Aadmi Party leader and Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal tell women not to serve dinner to their husbands if they "chant" Prime Minister Narendra Modi's name?
Answer: This shows the desperation of Arvind Kejriwal. AAP will be in contention to win just 20 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha election and it will be extremely difficult for AAP to win double digit seats. Narendra Modi is the front runner to win the next Lok Sabha election. The so called opposition alliance “INDIA” has unraveled. JD(U) and RLD have left the alliance and TMC have not left a single seat for Congress in West Bengal. Kejriwal is under extreme pressure to open its account in Lok Sabha from Delhi. Despite winning the last two assembly elections handsomely, AAP has failed to open their account in Delhi. Now, AAP has allied with its bitter political rival Congress in Delhi to fight BJP. AAP is also under pressure from Central agencies in the “Liquor Excise scam”. Any day Kejriwal can land in Tihar jail like his party leaders. In case, BJP manages to defeat the AAP-Congress alliance in all 7 seats in Delhi it will be huge embracement for Kejriwal. So, Kejriwal is showing desperation like announcing schemes to give Rs 1000 to every women in Delhi on the eve of Lok Sabha election. Now Kejriwal has gone to next step and asked “women not to serve dinner to their husbands if they "chant" Prime Minister Narendra Modi's name”. Kejriwal has to win at least one seat in Delhi to show his political mantle and I see this statement as a desperate act to fulfil this dream.

Question: What was your most embarrassing moment as a foreigner in another country?
Answer: It was 2018 or 2019. I was travelling from Amsterdam to Eindhoven in the Netherlands via train. It was a double decker train operated by NS. I went to the upper deck and sat on a seat. After a few minutes, I received a call from a friend and I started talking. Suddenly I realized that everyone was looking at me but I ignored. A person approached me after a few minutes and asked me to go out of the seating area and then talk on the phone. I confidently asked - “What is wrong in talking on a phone in the train”. He politely pointed out to a sign. The signboard was similar to the photo like this. Then I realized that I was sitting in the silent area. I was very embarrassed as there is no concept of silent coaches in Indian trains. I apologized to the person and others and then went outside the sitting area to talk with my friend. It was a very embarrassing moment for me.
